Adjustment 01

Two compact choices

Steer and Follow up now use two single-line rows. The explanation is available on hover, and keyboard selection still returns focus to the composer.

Look for: The menu is 164 points wide with two 28-point rows, down from 272 by 104 points.

Compact send choices in light mode, minimum window size

Compact send choices in dark mode, minimum window size

Adjustment 02

Room around the usage rings

The usage rings sit in their own strip below the composer. Model, context and send controls retain their space inside the box.

Look for: The ring strip stays below the composer while the model panel opens above its control.

Separate usage rings and model controls in light mode

Separate usage rings and model controls in dark mode

Adjustment 03

The same user-message surface

Follow-up and steer messages use the same black surface as regular user messages in light mode, and the same white surface in dark mode. Their symbols and accent edges remain distinct.

Look for: Compare the two delivered messages in both themes. The final capture shows the same treatment while messages are queued.

Delivered follow-up and steer messages in light mode

Delivered follow-up and steer messages in dark mode

Regular, follow-up and steer messages share the white dark-mode surface

Native checks

Checked the send and model panels at minimum size in both themes, selected both send modes, sent and delivered queued messages, and opened a usage ring. Send-menu Escape and composer focus return passed. The original macOS Auto appearance setting was restored.

Limits

The session uses a local RPC fixture. Usage details opened and closed with their Close button; Escape did not dismiss that separate panel. Full-suite timing and baseline screenshot failures remain recorded in the evidence report. The earlier gallery retains the first five adjustments.

Source: codex/active-session-ui-refinements at a78f90d610c6. PR #46 remains draft. Full results and remaining gaps are in README.md and density-verification.json.
